gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-tagbanwa: Noto Sans Tagbanwa keeps its curves open and its lowercase filling most of the line height, friendly and modern. Autour One sits above it, bold and expressive, with uninterrupted monoline strokes that give each heading a poster-like punch.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Expressive from the first word, Autour One draws round letters with no hairline-to-stem shift and barely any step down from capitals. Noto Sans Tai Tham follows in a contemporary sans, chalk-board lowercase easy to settle into.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-tai-viet: Autour One keeps its curves and stems in lockstep, a monoweight look with real swagger. Noto Sans Tai Viet follows in approachable, businesslike lowercase, with ascenders kept low and terminals pulled back from each curve, so paragraphs read smoothly and without strain.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-thai-l: Almendra Display brings an ornate, literary voice, its pronounced x-height and open letters feeling almost handwritten. And Noto Sans Thai Looped answers in sturdy sans-serif lowercase, its spacious curve terminals giving the heading room to perform.
gen-flavors-gf-noto-sans-tamil-supplemen: Noto Sans Tamil Supplement fills its middle band so fully that lines look stocky, with rounded shapes curving like parentheses. Flavors is the whimsical show-off, cut as if from strips of equal width; the body simply gets on with reading.
gen-almendra-display-gf-noto-sans-vai: Noto Sans Vai sets words as solid blocks, not skylines. Almendra Display on top adds an ornate, literary flourish, and the body underneath keeps generous gaps so the page stays modern and friendly.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Eater is dark and aggressive, its thin strokes beside moderately weighty stems and wide gaps between letters, with ascenders kept short. Noto Sans Thaana settles beneath it, approachable and plain sans, with big open lowercase.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Bold from the first glance, Autour One draws curves with no pinching at all. Noto Sans Tirhuta then carries a longer read gracefully, its terminals cut back to leave big gaps and its dominant x-height keeping text easy on the eye.
gen-gf-autour-one-gf-noto-sans-warang-ci: Autour One has a pencil-line consistency, expressive and bold, with round letters that flow smoothly into stems. And Noto Sans Warang Citi, a sans-serif with solid word blocks, gives wide channels into every counter; bigger headings than body text suit it.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-zanabazar-square: Noto Sans Zanabazar Square has a soaring x-height and wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp. And Eater, dark and aggressive above it, swings mellowly from thick to thin, so paragraphs below feel approachable and easy.
